transcript.text: Our Samsung combi microwave keeps whirring for a few minutes after it's finished and beeped, even with the door open. Old one never did that. Is the fan stuck on?

That's almost certainly normal. Most combi microwaves, including Samsung's, have a cooling fan that keeps running after cooking finishes. Samsung's manuals mention it as expected behaviour.

Why it happens

• Combi models have a grill and/or convection heater as well as the microwave magnetron, so they get much hotter inside than a basic microwave.
• The fan cools the electronics, magnetron and casing, not the food compartment. That's why opening the door doesn't stop it.
• It usually runs longer after grill, convection or combination cooking than after plain microwave use.
• Your old microwave was probably a simpler solo model that didn't build up as much heat, so it didn't need to do this.

What's normal

• The fan runs for a few minutes (sometimes up to 5 to 10 after a long grill or convection session) and then switches itself off.
• It sounds like a steady whir, similar to the noise during cooking.

When it might actually be a fault

• It never stops, or keeps running for well over 15 minutes.
• It starts on its own when you haven't used the oven.
• It makes grinding, rattling or squealing noises.
• You notice a burning smell or see an error code on the display.

If any of those happen, unplug it for a minute or two to reset it. If the problem continues, contact Samsung support or a repair service, especially if it's still under warranty.

Tips

• Let it finish rather than unplugging it to stop it, since it's protecting the components.
• Keep the vents clear and leave the clearance around the oven that the manual recommends, so it can cool efficiently.
